content.bio:
/**
 * Обо мне
 * Я Frontend Lead в SaaS-компании. Делаю SaaS-продукты
 * на React, Next.js и TypeScript.

 * {years, plural, one {# год} few {# года} many {# лет} other {# года}} во фронтенде. Начал инженером

 * и вёл людей, которые их строят.

content.interests:
/**
 * Интересы
 * Я проактивный человек, нацеленный на рост. 
 * Люблю решать сложные задачи и выстраивать 
 * сотрудничество в командах. Убеждён, что поддерживающая 
 * среда, дающая людям силу действовать, — залог 
 * успеха и в жизни, и в работе.
 *
 * Мой фокус — постоянное саморазвитие, инновации 
 * и гибкость. Мне нравятся сложные проблемы, 
 * новые технологии и творческие решения, к которым я 
 * подталкиваю команду.
 *
 * Я ценю открытое общение, доверие и прозрачность 
 * и забочусь об атмосфере, где каждый может предложить 
 * идею и расти.
 *
 * Меня движут любопытство, любовь к работе, которая 
 * влияет на результат, и желание менять вещи к лучшему — 
 * и как лидера, и как человека.
 */

content.games:
/**
 * Games
 * I play World of Warcraft and whatever is new on
 * my PS5. I also like how games are built: a tight
 * loop of input, state and feedback is good practice
 * for frontend thinking.
 *
 * I am building two of my own:
 * Tiny Coop, a cozy idle desktop game about a hen,
 * made in Godot 4 and heading to Steam.
 * Dareboard, a party game app (truth or dare, never
 * have I ever, spin the bottle) in Expo and React
 * Native, coming to the App Store and Google Play.
 *
 * The snake on the home page is a small one: a pure
 * state engine, testable without a canvas.
 */
content.learning:
/**
 * Learning
 * I am self-taught. I learned frontend from
 * documentation, source code and real projects,
 * and I still learn the same way.
 *
 * Frontend changes fast, and so does the way teams
 * work. I try new ideas in small side projects
 * before they reach a team.
 *
 * This site is one of them: Feature-Sliced Design,
 * strict lint rules and a GSAP motion toolkit.
 *
 * Later I taught others: I lectured JavaScript and
 * React to students at an IT school.
 */

step.details: One tick of the snake engine: a pure function from the previous state to the next, so the game logic is testable without a canvas. It moves the head, grows on food and ends the round on a wall or self hit (the excerpt keeps the move and the eating).

keyToDirection.details: Maps a key press to a snake direction. Arrow keys and WASD both work, and shortcuts with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt held are ignored so the game never steals browser shortcuts.

early-stage-products.summary: Headed the frontend side of a few young products. Shaped app foundations they could share and scripted the repetitive parts of starting a project.

data-heavy-ui.title: _data-heavy-ui
data-heavy-ui.summary: Rebuilt key screens and wrote interactive widgets that draw custom graphics from live data. Simplified how users move through the product.

ecommerce-platform.title: _ecommerce-platform
ecommerce-platform.summary: Ran frontend for online storefronts with many sellers. Packaged a starter setup in React so new projects began from a working base.

client-apps.title: _client-apps
client-apps.summary: Delivered interfaces for several customer products on top of Python backends. Extracted common UI parts and helped newer colleagues get productive.

lead-automation.title: _lead-automation
lead-automation.summary: Wired company websites to the sales pipeline so inquiries were routed without manual work, added chat-bot helpers for the team, and sped up page loads.

dareboard.summary: Party game app: truth or dare, never have I ever, spin the bottle. Expo client, NestJS API and an Astro landing page. Coming to the App Store and Google Play.
